hooks.name: Smart Git Commit
hooks.description: When a session ends, review the git diff, write a descriptive conventional commit message, show it to the user, and only commit after getting explicit approval.

action.prompt:
Before ending, check if there are any uncommitted changes by running `git status --short` in the workspace. If there are changes:

1. Run `git diff` (and `git diff --cached` if anything is staged) to understand what was changed.
2. Write a single-line git commit message following conventional commit style (e.g. feat:, fix:, refactor:, docs:, chore:). Keep it under 72 characters. No body, no bullet points — just one clear line.
3. Present the proposed commit message to the user and explicitly ask for their permission before committing.
4. Only if the user approves, stage all changes with `git add -A` and commit with the approved message.
5. If the user declines or wants edits, follow their instructions.

Do NOT commit without user approval. Do NOT use a generic message like "Auto-commit: changes from Kiro session". Always keep the commit message to a single line.
